questions.q: How do PySpark and Scala Spark compare as Glue job authoring languages?
options: Both compile down to the same underlying Spark engine — the choice is mostly about team preference and ecosystem fit
Scala Spark jobs run on Glue while PySpark jobs require a separate EMR cluster
PySpark cannot read from the Data Catalog, only Scala can
They produce fundamentally different, incompatible output data
questions.explain: Both languages run on the same Spark execution engine underneath — the practical ETL capability is nearly identical.

questions.q: What does calling job.commit() at the end of a generated Glue script actually do?
options: It finalizes the job run, including committing bookmark state for incremental reruns
It permanently deletes the source data after processing
It compiles the PySpark script into Scala
It has no functional effect and exists only for readability
questions.explain: job.commit() finalizes the run and bookmark state — skipping it breaks correct behavior on subsequent incremental runs.

questions.q: What is a DynamicFrame designed for, compared to a standard Spark DataFrame?
options: Semi-structured data where schema might vary row to row, such as messy real-world JSON
Only data that is already perfectly typed and consistent
Exclusively binary image data
Data stored only in Redshift, never in S3
questions.explain: DynamicFrames tolerate schema variation across records, which is common in semi-structured sources like JSON.

questions.q: In the typical DynamicFrame/DataFrame workflow this lesson describes, when do you convert with .toDF()?
options: After reading a DynamicFrame from the Catalog, to run standard Spark transform logic on a DataFrame
Before the job has read any data at all
Only when writing final output back to the Catalog
Never — DynamicFrames and DataFrames cannot be converted between each other
questions.explain: The common pattern is: read into a DynamicFrame, convert with .toDF() for transform logic, then convert back with fromDF() if needed for Glue-specific writes.

questions.q: How does a typical Glue job read its source data, per this lesson's example?
options: By database and table name from the Data Catalog, via create_dynamic_frame.from_catalog
By hardcoding a specific EC2 file path
Only through a manually pasted schema definition in the script
By connecting directly to the source application's production database
questions.explain: Jobs typically read via the Catalog by database/table name rather than a hardcoded S3 path, relying on the crawler-then-job pattern.
